text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- The number of guests at the Slovenian coast this weekend was 11 percent higher than in the same period of last year, tourist statistics showed.
- Most Slovenian school children will end the 1996/97 school year next week.
- Parliament did not grant immunity to Zmago Jelincic, the president of the Nationalist Party, who was indicted for insulting Pavel Domitrica, a consultant at the parliament.
- The government and parliament have yet to approve the 1997 programme of the state Highway Company, which oversees the construction of new motorways in Slovenia.

- Macroeconomic stability in the former socialist countries is the main factor to help reduce unemployment in the area, said participants at an international conference on unemployment in the coastal town of Portoroz this weekend.

- Retail prices in Slovenia are about 64 percent higher than in Slovakia and 57 percent higher than in Poland, but because of higher salaries, purchasing power in Slovenia is still higher than in both countries, Slovenia's Institute for Economic Diagnosis and Prognosis said.
- Cveto Koder, a member of the conservative People's Party, became mayor of the city of Idrija in the second round of local elections on Sunday.
- Experts said Slovenia should officially recognise homeopathic treatment in line with other European Union countries. Currently, homeopathy is illegal in Slovenia.
